# Fabric notebook handover: provisioning and Oracle target changes

This is an implementation brief for the coding agent building the **Fabric
PySpark notebook**. It describes the live application contract, Config DB,
connections, each approved action, and the exact result expected by the API.
The implementation is saved as
[`nb_migration_provisioning.py`](nb_migration_provisioning.py) and
[`nb_migration_provisioning.ipynb`](nb_migration_provisioning.ipynb). The user
reported Fabric notebook item ID `5b8a6415-f6b9-4890-8bc5-226528914c59`.
The repository copy fixes the exported notebook's hardcoded parameter GUID,
approval comparison, and ingestion flag handling. Upload this copy over the
Fabric item before an app-driven run; the local edit does not change the
deployed Fabric notebook. Its local self-tests pass, but a Fabric DEV run is
still required to verify connections and Delta operations. All four target
actions are implemented in this copy. `ALTER_BACKFILL` and `REPLACE_FULL`
require [`003_target_change_runs.sql`](../configdb/migrations/003_target_change_runs.sql),
`python-oracledb` in the Fabric environment, an idle replication batch, and
an Oracle maintenance window. Their local tests use fakes; live execution
has not been verified.
The notebook probes `SHOW TABLES IN <lakehouse>.<schema>` before relying on
`SHOW SCHEMAS IN <lakehouse>`. In Fabric, the table listing can succeed even
when that schema listing raises `SCHEMA_NOT_FOUND`; treating the latter as
proof of an absent table caused a false `ALTER_FUTURE requires the physical
table to exist` failure. Deploy this updated notebook code to the Fabric item
before starting another workflow for that action.
The app submits new `CHANGE_REQUESTED` plans to the notebook when a notebook ID
is selected. An earlier closed approval stays recorded; a new Oracle migration
workflow is needed for a fresh approval and execution. Successful notebook
execution sets the change plan to `CHANGE_APPLIED`; it does not create a second
`SourceTables` row or run the replication pipeline.

## 1. Current application behavior

The FastAPI/Temporal app sends a notebook job for a **new** approved plan with
one Text parameter, `plan_guid`. See `thirdparty/fabric/client.py` and
`app/migration/fabric_activities.py`. Runtime rows for a new plan already exist
in Config DB. The worker marks them provisioned after the notebook reports
success. The workflow stores the parsed notebook report in its state, and the
thin UI shows it under **Provisioning report**.

For an **existing** Oracle target, the app compares the proposed structure with
active **Config DB records**, including `PENDING` records. An identical
recorded structure ends as `DUPLICATE_TARGET`. A changed structure opens a
separate UI approval and saves a `CHANGE_REQUESTED` plan. That approval has no
new `SourceTables` row. When a notebook ID is selected, the app submits it
after approval and stores the notebook's object report.

The recorded comparison is **not a physical Fabric schema check**. The
notebook must inspect the Delta table and stop if its schema differs from the
recorded baseline.

## 2. Notebook parameter cell

Create a PySpark code cell and select **Mark cell as parameters** in Fabric:

```python
# Parameter cell; the job overrides the default.
plan_guid = ""
```

| Parameter | Required | Type | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plan_guid` | Yes | Text UUID | The API submits `MigrationPlans.PlanGUID`. |

This is the **only parameter the app currently sends**. Validate that it is a
UUID and require exactly one matching approved plan. Do not accept `action`,
table name, schema, target workspace, watermark, or credentials as extra job
parameters. Read those from the approved plan in Config DB so a caller cannot
override a user's decision.

The REST submission body generated by the current client contains:

```json
{"parameters":[{"name":"plan_guid","value":"<plan UUID>","type":"Text"}]}
```

## 3. Required return status and detailed report

Exit with **one JSON string**. The result parser now accepts this shape:

```json
{
  "status": "SUCCESS",
  "plan_guid": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "tables_processed": 1,
  "views_processed": 1,
  "duration_seconds": 83.42,
  "objects": [
    {
      "object_type": "TABLE",
      "name": "LOCAL_ORACLE.SALES_ORDER_HEADER",
      "status": "SUCCESS",
      "duration_seconds": 71.20,
      "started_at": "2026-10-01T12:00:00Z",
      "completed_at": "2026-10-01T12:01:11.200Z",
      "rows_written": 125000,
      "message": "Schema and row count validated"
    },
    {
      "object_type": "VIEW",
      "name": "LOCAL_ORACLE.SALES_ORDER_HEADER_V",
      "status": "SUCCESS",
      "duration_seconds": 12.22,
      "started_at": "2026-10-01T12:01:11.200Z",
      "completed_at": "2026-10-01T12:01:23.420Z",
      "message": "View created and queried"
    }
  ],
  "message": "Provisioning completed"
}
```

`status` must be `SUCCESS` or `FAILED`; `plan_guid` must match the input.
`tables_processed` and `views_processed` are nonnegative counts of **successful
objects**. For a new plan the worker checks them against its planned table and
view count. If `objects` is present, its successful TABLE/VIEW counts must
match these totals. An overall `SUCCESS` cannot include a `FAILED` or
`SKIPPED` object. Each object needs `object_type`, qualified `name`, `status`,
and nonnegative `duration_seconds`. Optional fields are `started_at`,
`completed_at`, nonnegative `rows_written`, and a safe `message`. Overall
`duration_seconds` is nonnegative. The parser lives in
`services/fabric_provisioning.py` and rejects unknown fields.

On a known failure, return `status: "FAILED"`, the matching `plan_guid`,
successful object counts so far, and object statuses including the failed
object. Keep error text concise and secret-free. A crash before exit also
fails the Fabric job. Never return `SUCCESS` for a pending write, unverified
schema, or incomplete Config DB operation.

Example failure exit string:

```json
{
  "status": "FAILED",
  "plan_guid": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
  "tables_processed": 0,
  "views_processed": 0,
  "duration_seconds": 14.3,
  "objects": [
    {"object_type":"TABLE","name":"LOCAL_ORACLE.SALES_ORDER_HEADER",
     "status":"FAILED","duration_seconds":14.3,
     "message":"Physical schema differs from approved baseline"}
  ],
  "message": "Target change was not applied"
}
```

Use `notebookutils.notebook.exit(json.dumps(result))` in its **own final cell at
top level**, outside `try/except`. Fabric documents that wrapping `exit()` in
`try/except` can prevent it from taking effect. Record object times with a
monotonic timer, and UTC timestamps for the report.

## 4. Configuration database and connection details

Config DB is a **Fabric SQL database**, separate from the target Lakehouse.
Its display name is `AutoMigrationConfigDB`. In the current environment its
actual SQL catalog is
`AutoMigrationConfigDB-0187c7e0-422b-4e81-8c5b-19826692a2a4`.
The catalog suffix can change if the database item is recreated. Obtain the
server and current catalog from the SQL database item's **connection string**
in Fabric (or the local app's `CONFIG_DB_URL`). Use the SQL **database**
endpoint, not the Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint. The current app uses
port 1433, encryption, and `ActiveDirectoryServicePrincipal` authentication.

The notebook cannot read the local `.env`. Configure its own identity with
access to the SQL database item and SQL permissions on the
`bronze_replication` schema. The app uses `mssql-python>=1.11.0`; install it
in the Fabric notebook environment if needed. For transactional multi-table
updates, use the SQL driver. Store its service principal client ID/secret in
Azure Key Vault and retrieve them at runtime. This is a **template** with
placeholders, never a credential to paste verbatim:

```python
import mssql_python
from notebookutils import credentials

vault_url = "https://<vault-name>.vault.azure.net/"
sql_server = "<copy SQL server from Fabric database connection string>"
sql_catalog = "AutoMigrationConfigDB-0187c7e0-422b-4e81-8c5b-19826692a2a4"
client_id = credentials.getSecret(vault_url, "configdb-client-id")
client_secret = credentials.getSecret(vault_url, "configdb-client-secret")

sql_connection_string = (
    f"Server={sql_server};Database={sql_catalog};"
    "Authentication=ActiveDirectoryServicePrincipal;"
    f"UID={client_id};PWD={client_secret};"
    "Encrypt=yes;TrustServerCertificate=no;"
)
db = mssql_python.connect(sql_connection_string, timeout=30)
```

Do not print the connection string, tokens, `ConnectionDetails`, or SQL
exception text containing credentials. Verify access using a nonsecret query
such as `SELECT DB_NAME()`. Test under the background job identity as well as
in an interactive notebook. Close connections/cursors. Use bound `?` values
for all SQL parameters, transactions for coordinated updates, and affected
row-count checks. The notebook's service principal needs Fabric item access
and database read/write privileges for the required tables.

For read-heavy queries, Fabric's preinstalled Spark SQL connector can read
the SQL database with a URL like
`jdbc:sqlserver://<server>:1433;database=<catalog>;` and Entra identity.
Its independent DataFrame writes are **not** a replacement for one SQL
transaction across Config DB tables.

The source DDL is `thirdparty/configdb/config_db_new_database.sql`. The app's
connection helper is `thirdparty/configdb/utils.py::ConfigDB`; its typed
repository is `thirdparty/configdb/repository.py`.

## 5. Config DB tables and exact relationships

All names below are in SQL schema `bronze_replication`.

| Table | Key fields | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MigrationPlans` | `PlanGUID`, `PlanVersion`, `Status`, `ApprovedBy`, `ApprovedTimestamp`, `Notes`, `RuntimePlanHash` | Approval and plan identity. Change JSON is in `Notes`. |
| `SourceTables` | `GUID`, `PlanGUID`, `ConnectionName`, source schema/table, target workspace/lakehouse ID, target schema/table, `ProvisioningStatus`, `IsActive` | Existing target record and target identity. |
| `SourceTableColumns` | `SourceTableColumnGUID`, `GUID` (FK to `SourceTables.GUID`), `Sno`, source/target names, source/Fabric types, nullability, key flags | Recorded source and target schema. |
| `ReplicationConfig` | `SourceTableGUID` unique, incremental method, watermark column/type/index, write strategy, JSON key arrays, `IngestionFlag` | Queue and merge behavior. |
| `ReplicationState` | `SourceTableGUID` PK, `LastWatermarkValue`, run IDs, row counts, `Status` | Current incremental progress. |
| `DBConnections` | unique `ConnectionName`, `SourceType`, `ConnectionDetails` JSON, `IsActive` | Oracle endpoint and current app-stored Oracle credentials. |
| `BatchRuns`, `BatchObjectRuns` | batch/job and per-object statuses | Worker audit for new plans. A change-run audit does not exist yet. |

`SourceTables.GUID` is the stable existing target ID. It equals the FK used by
`SourceTableColumns.GUID`, `ReplicationConfig.SourceTableGUID`, and
`ReplicationState.SourceTableGUID`. A **change plan has no new SourceTables row**.
For a change, use `Notes.target_change.existing_source_table_guid`, not
`SourceTables WHERE PlanGUID=<change plan_guid>`.

The global replication view `vw_ReplicationQueue` selects every active,
`PROVISIONED` row with `IngestionFlag=1`. It has **no plan GUID filter**. Keep
one active configuration for each target and pause ingestion during alteration
or backfill.

### Required lookups (parameterized SQL)

```sql
SELECT PlanGUID, PlanVersion, Status, ApprovedBy, ApprovedTimestamp,
       RuntimePlanHash, Notes
FROM bronze_replication.MigrationPlans WHERE PlanGUID = ?;

SELECT GUID, PlanGUID, ConnectionName, SourceSystemType, SourceSchemaName,
       SourceTableName, FabricWorkspaceId, FabricLakehouseId,
       FabricLakehouseSchema, FabricTableName, IsActive, ProvisioningStatus
FROM bronze_replication.SourceTables WHERE GUID = ?;

SELECT Sno, ColumnName, TargetColumnName, SourceDataType, FabricDataType,
       IsNullable, IsPrimaryKey, IsSelected
FROM bronze_replication.SourceTableColumns WHERE GUID = ? ORDER BY Sno;

SELECT IncrementalMethod, WatermarkColumn, WatermarkColumnDataType,
       WatermarkIndexName, WriteStrategy, PrimaryKeyColumns, MergeKeyColumns,
       IngestionFlag, PipelineWorkspaceId, PipelineItemId
FROM bronze_replication.ReplicationConfig WHERE SourceTableGUID = ?;

SELECT LastWatermarkValue, LastSuccessfulBatchRunId, LastPipelineRunId,
       LastSuccessfulTimestamp, Status
FROM bronze_replication.ReplicationState WHERE SourceTableGUID = ?;

SELECT SourceType, ConnectionDetails, IsActive
FROM bronze_replication.DBConnections WHERE ConnectionName = ?;
```

For a **new** plan load its runtime tables using `SourceTables.PlanGUID = ?`.
For a **change** plan require `Status='CHANGE_REQUESTED'`, parse `Notes`, and
load the existing target row by GUID. Re-read all rows just before writing so
the decision is applied to current state, not stale notebook memory.

      "replication": {

This is an illustrative **subset**. The actual stored plan contains all model
fields in snake_case. Parse and validate it rather than assuming the example
has every property. Require exact agreement among the target in `review`,
`proposed_plan.table`, and the live `SourceTables` row. Recalculate the diff
against current recorded columns; stop if it differs from approval. The
`physical_schema_verified` flag is currently `false` by design.

## 7. Oracle source connection for backfill or full reload

Get the active Oracle `DBConnections` row named by
`proposed_plan.table.connection_name`. Require `SourceType='ORACLE'`.
Current UI-created `ConnectionDetails` contains either:

```json
{"dsn":"db.example.com:1521/service","username":"<user>","password":"<secret>"}
```

or:

```json
{"host":"db.example.com","port":1521,"serviceName":"service",
 "username":"<user>","password":"<secret>"}
```

The SQL DDL comment calls this JSON non-secret metadata, but the **current
application stores the Oracle username and password in it**. Restrict SQL
permissions accordingly. Never put these values in notebook parameters,
Temporal history, `MigrationPlans.Notes`, logs, object report messages, or
exit JSON. A later revision can store a Key Vault reference instead.

`python-oracledb` Thin mode can connect without Instant Client if the source
supports it and the Fabric runtime can reach Oracle. The local app's Oracle
adapter uses **Thick** mode, so do not assume it can be copied unchanged to
Fabric. Example for a compatible source:

```python
import json
import oracledb

details = json.loads(connection_details_from_db)
dsn = details.get("dsn") or (
    f"{details['host']}:{details.get('port', 1521)}/{details['serviceName']}"
)
oracle = oracledb.connect(user=details["username"],
                          password=details["password"], dsn=dsn)
```

Verify network reachability first, especially for private/on-premises Oracle.
If the Fabric notebook cannot reach it, use an approved ingestion route with
the needed network/gateway access. Read in bounded chunks or Spark partitions;
do not collect the full table in driver memory. Validate schema/table/column
identifiers against discovered metadata and bind SQL values.

For data-changing actions, the Oracle user must be able to read the table,
execute `DBMS_FLASHBACK.GET_SYSTEM_CHANGE_NUMBER`, and lock the source table
in `SHARE` mode. The notebook uses `NOWAIT`: if another writer holds an
incompatible lock, it reports `FAILED` before touching the Delta target.

## 8. Physical schema inspection and decision rules

Attach the notebook to the **target Lakehouse** or explicitly address the
approved workspace/lakehouse. Verify its IDs. Read the **Spark Delta** table
schema and Delta version. Do not use the Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint for
DDL. For a schema-enabled Lakehouse, use a safely quoted qualified table such
as `` `LOCAL_ORACLE`.`SALES_ORDER_HEADER` ``. Never splice unchecked names
into `ALTER TABLE`, `MERGE`, or `CREATE OR REPLACE` SQL.

Compare (1) recorded existing `SourceTableColumns`, (2) physical Delta
columns/types/nullability, and (3) approved proposed columns. Normalize
equivalent type aliases and identifier case deliberately. Treat SQL
`IsNullable=NULL` as **unknown**. If recorded and physical schemas differ,
stop and request a fresh review. Recheck immediately before DDL/commit and
serialize writers for that target.

| Decision | Preconditions | Allowed effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `REVISE_PLANNED` | Existing row `PENDING`; no physical target table | Revise the single active saved configuration; no Spark DDL. |
| `ALTER_FUTURE` | Existing row `PROVISIONED`; physical table exists | Add nullable columns and individually verified safe type widening. Old rows remain unchanged. |
| `ALTER_BACKFILL` | Same physical checks; stable merge key | Apply safe schema changes, scan historical Oracle data, and merge old rows. |
| `REPLACE_FULL` | Existing physical table and full source snapshot available | Build and validate replacement data, then atomically replace table data/schema. |

The UI currently allows an alter choice even when a diff contains removals or
incompatible type changes. The notebook must reject that action with
`FAILED`, not silently turn it into a replacement. Verify type widening
against the actual Delta runtime and table protocol.

### `REVISE_PLANNED`

Require `PENDING`, no physical table, and a still-active old record. In one
Config DB transaction update its columns and replication configuration, or
supersede it and insert exactly one replacement record. Preserve audit links
and ensure no duplicate active queue entry. No Oracle read or Spark write is
needed. The app still needs a completion transition for the change plan.

### `ALTER_FUTURE`

Pause ingestion, capture `IngestionFlag` and old watermark, and acquire a
durable target lease. Recheck physical schema. Execute approved `ALTER TABLE
... ADD COLUMNS` and only verified widenings. Reject dropped/renamed columns,
narrowing, key changes, and incompatible nullability. Verify new physical
schema; update the **existing** Config DB column/config rows in one SQL
transaction. Keep `LastWatermarkValue` unchanged. Resume ingestion only after
physical and Config DB validation. Unchanged historical rows can have `NULL`
in newly added columns; future watermark updates may populate updated rows.

### `ALTER_BACKFILL`

Apply the same safe schema alteration, then **explicitly reread historical
Oracle rows**. Resetting `LastWatermarkValue` alone is not a backfill: old
unchanged rows may never reappear. Require a stable approved primary/merge
key; otherwise fail and request `REPLACE_FULL` approval.

1. Pause ingestion and refuse to proceed while `ReplicationState.Status` is
   `RUNNING`. Take an Oracle `LOCK TABLE ... IN SHARE MODE NOWAIT` and capture
   an SCN. Hold that lock through the Config DB commit. Source writes are
   blocked during this operation, so schedule a maintenance window.
2. Read the complete table `AS OF SCN` in fetches of 5,000 rows and write a
   plan-specific staging Delta table. A retry before target mutation rebuilds
   the stage from the beginning; this version has no chunk resume checkpoint.
3. Cast every value to its approved `fabric_data_type`; validate key
   uniqueness, rejected casts, nullability, and source/target counts.
4. `MERGE` by key into Delta and verify every staged row is present with the
   approved values. No source writes can occur while the Oracle lock is held.
5. Update Config DB metadata in one transaction and keep the previous
   watermark. The unchanged `WATERMARK/UPSERT` pipeline may safely replay
   from that older position.
6. Restore the original ingestion flag in the same transaction. If target
   mutation may have started and a step fails, leave ingestion paused and
   require reconciliation before retrying.

### `REPLACE_FULL`

Pause ingestion and hold the Oracle `SHARE` lock through the Config DB commit.
Extract a full `AS OF SCN` snapshot to a **staging Delta table**, validate
types and row count, then use `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ... AS SELECT` to replace
the target schema and data. Verify the resulting schema and data against the
stage before committing metadata. Keep the previous watermark for replay if
replication is `WATERMARK/UPSERT`; `FULL/REPLACE` continues to use full loads.
Only these unchanged replication mode pairs are supported. The staging table
is retained for recovery.

## 9. Config DB transaction, concurrency, and retry behavior

Spark/Delta and Config DB cannot share one distributed transaction. Apply
`thirdparty/configdb/migrations/003_target_change_runs.sql` to create the
durable `TargetChangeRuns` record. It stores the plan, target, action, staging
name, SCN, source row count, and phase. The notebook also takes a per-target
SQL application lock. It does not hold a Config DB transaction across Spark
work.

For the same `plan_guid`, only `STARTED` and `STAGED` may retry automatically;
the stage is rebuilt from a new locked Oracle snapshot. `MUTATION_STARTED`
is recorded **before** the first target write. An uncertain retry then stops
for operator reconciliation. Use the existing `SourceTables.GUID`; keep only
one active queue entry. Column and replication metadata plus ingestion state
are updated transactionally. `ReplicationState.LastWatermarkValue` is left
unchanged for safe replay.

If Delta commits but Config DB fails, the `MUTATION_STARTED` record and staging
table remain; ingestion stays disabled and the result is `FAILED`. Inspect the
actual Delta schema/data and Config DB before manually reconciling. The
notebook will not blindly replay DDL or data movement.
Do not include credentials or raw source rows in the report.

## 10. Suggested notebook cell structure

1. **Parameter cell:** `plan_guid = ""`, marked as parameters.
2. **Imports/config:** standard library, `mssql_python`, `oracledb` if needed,
   Spark, and `notebookutils`. Set nonsecret SQL server/catalog/vault URI.
3. **Load/validate plan:** query Config DB; detect new plan versus
   `CHANGE_REQUESTED`; parse approved proposal and target identity.
4. **Preflight:** load existing records, Oracle connection only if required,
   physical Spark schema/version, diff, permissions, lease.
5. **Execute:** dispatch exactly one approved action; record per-object
   start/end time, rows written, and safe result message.
6. **Verify/commit:** inspect final physical schema and data, commit Config DB
   updates for change mode, release lease, build overall report.
7. **Exit cell:** `notebookutils.notebook.exit(json.dumps(result))` at top level.

For new-plan mode, leave `finish_provisioning` writes to the Temporal worker.
For change mode, do not call that activity as currently written: it expects
runtime rows owned by the change plan, but there are none.

## 11. DEV acceptance tests

| Scenario | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Missing, blank, malformed, or unapproved `plan_guid` | `FAILED`; no mutation. |
| New target | Approved table/view provisioned; report lists each successful object and elapsed time; worker accepts counts. |
| Stale recorded or physical schema | `FAILED`; no DDL. |
| `REVISE_PLANNED` with no physical table | One active revised config; no Spark write. |
| `ALTER_FUTURE` adds a nullable column | Old rows unchanged; recorded/physical schemas match; watermark unchanged. |
| Removal or unsafe type conversion under alter | `FAILED`; no silent replacement. |
| `ALTER_BACKFILL` with old unchanged rows | Values populated via merge, no duplicate keys, old watermark retained for replay. |
| Interrupted backfill before target mutation | Stage rebuilt from a fresh locked snapshot. |
| Interrupted backfill after `MUTATION_STARTED` | Retry blocked; ingestion paused for reconciliation. |
| `REPLACE_FULL` staging validation failure | Original target remains; report names failed object and time. |
| Delta succeeds but Config DB fails | `FAILED` with `MUTATION_STARTED` run record; ingestion stays paused. |
| Concurrent jobs on same target | At most one acquires the target lease. |
| Report counts disagree with object list | App parser rejects the result. |

## 12. App integration and run sequence

For a new Oracle workflow, select the provisioning notebook before starting.
After the target change approval, the workflow validates the saved
`CHANGE_REQUESTED` plan, submits its PlanGUID to the notebook, waits for the
Fabric job, parses the object report, and moves the plan to `CHANGE_APPLIED`
after one successful table result. The thin UI displays the returned report.

An older workflow that already closed at `CHANGE_REQUESTED` will not resume
when the worker restarts. Start a new workflow to use this automatic path.

`TargetChangeRuns` records notebook data movement. The change path uses
`finish_target_change`, not `finish_provisioning`, because a change PlanGUID
does not own the existing SourceTables row. This path does not automatically
run the replication pipeline or enable an existing table's replication config;
that requires physical and metadata reconciliation after the notebook change.
If a Fabric submission outcome is uncertain, reconcile its job ID before
retrying submission.
